questions.explanation: 'Going to' for predictions based on present evidence (the clouds).
questions.q: Look at those clouds! It ___.

questions.explanation: 'Going to' for a decision already made / a plan.
questions.q: I've decided — I ___ study medicine next year.

questions.explanation: 'Will' for an instant decision / offer made now.
questions.q: A: I've got a headache. B: ___ you some aspirin.

questions.explanation: Present continuous for a fixed personal arrangement.
questions.q: We ___ our grandparents on Sunday — we called them yesterday.

questions.explanation: 'Will' for promises.
questions.q: I promise I ___ late again.

questions.explanation: Present simple for timetables and fixed schedules.
questions.q: The train ___ at 7:30 tomorrow morning.

questions.explanation: 'Will' + infinitive without 'to'.
options: I am go to help you.
questions.q: Which sentence is correct?

questions.explanation: 'Going to' for a prediction based on what we can see now.
questions.q: Watch out! You ___ your coffee!

questions.explanation: 'Will' for an instant decision made at the moment of speaking.
questions.q: A: The phone's ringing! B: ___ it.

questions.explanation: Present continuous for a fixed arrangement in the near future.
questions.q: They ___ married in June — the invitations are ready.

questions.explanation: 'Will' for predictions based on opinion, especially after 'I think'.
questions.q: I think it ___ tomorrow.

questions.explanation: Present continuous for an arrangement that is already fixed.
questions.q: We've bought the tickets, so we ___ to Rome in May.

questions.explanation: 'Will' for an instant decision.
questions.q: A: Someone's at the door. B: ___ see who it is.

questions.explanation: 'Going to' for a prediction based on present evidence.
questions.q: Look! That car ___ crash!

questions.explanation: Present continuous for asking about fixed plans.
questions.q: What ___ this evening?

questions.explanation: Present simple for timetables.
questions.q: Our flight ___ at 6 a.m. — don't be late!

questions.explanation: After 'will', use the infinitive without 'to' or '-s': 'will help'.
questions.q: Which sentence is WRONG?

questions.explanation: 'Will' for an offer decided at the moment of speaking.
questions.q: A: I'm really hungry. B: ___ you a sandwich.

questions.explanation: 'Going to' for a plan decided before now.
questions.q: They ___ a new house next year — they've already saved the money.

questions.explanation: Present continuous = be + verb+ing for future arrangements: 'are meeting'.
questions.q: Which of the following sentences is correct?

topic: Future forms (will / going to / present continuous)
